sets.title: Flash programming as a constrained state change

objective_text.T59.01.a: Derive and defend: Prove admission catches every forbidden bit transition and prevents a partially modified prefix. Derive physical program-unit alignment and erase-sector dependencies separately.
objective_text.T59.01.b: Implement and investigate: Implement lc_program(dst,src,n) on live disjoint octet spans: reject if any new byte requests a0-to-1 transition, leaving all bytes unchanged; otherwise program with bitwise AND. n0 succeeds. This is an atomic admission model, not a claim that physical multi-byte programming is atomic.
objective_text.T59.01.c: Falsify and transfer: Repair a model that silently ANDs an illegal request and reports success. Its resulting bytes differ from the requested image even without a crash. Then Replace whole-span admission by per-program-unit persistence and cut power after each unit; derive which metadata must stay uncommitted until image completion.

sets.title: Integrity without authenticity

objective_text.T59.02.a: Derive and defend: Derive one byte update by polynomial division and state the initialization/reflection/finalization conventions. Explain collision possibility and absence of a secret authentication key.
objective_text.T59.02.b: Implement and investigate: Implement lc_crc using reflected CRC-32 polynomial0xedb88320, initial state0xffffffff and final complement, processing bytes low-bit first. No CRC library. Verify empty input and123456789, then construct an altered payload with a recomputed checksum and explain why it still lacks authorization.
objective_text.T59.02.c: Falsify and transfer: A verifier omits the final complement and rejects valid images; another accepts attacker-recomputed CRC as a signature. Only the first defect is covered by numeric test anchors. Then Add a separately verified signature API that returns an explicit verdict and key identifier; inject fail-open and stale-key responses without implementing production cryptography in this exercise.

sets.title: Authenticated image admission

objective_text.T59.03.a: Derive and defend: Specify exactly which bytes and metadata the trusted verifier authenticates; derive bounded extent arithmetic and the immutable authority for the rollback floor.
objective_text.T59.03.b: Implement and investigate: Implement lc_admit(length,slot_capacity,version,floor,signature_ok): accept only length1..capacity, version>=floor and signature_ok exactly1. The verifier verdict is injected by the harness; it is not derived from a learner-controlled flag in a real image. Return0 for all invalid requests before any slot selection.
objective_text.T59.03.c: Falsify and transfer: The intentionally faulty admission ignores a failed verifier verdict. Harmless success is selection of a synthetic unauthorized image; no real key or deployed bootloader is targeted. Then Introduce key rotation and a revoked signing key; show why a numerically newer version with a valid old-key signature may still be inadmissible.

sets.title: Trial boot, confirmation and rollback

objective_text.T59.04.a: Derive and defend: Prove repeated unconfirmed resets eventually return to a known confirmed slot. Identify the exact persistence point before transferring control and the risk if it occurs afterward.
objective_text.T59.04.b: Implement and investigate: Implement lc_select on LCBoot with active and trial slots0/1, confirmed and attempted booleans. If confirmed select active. If unconfirmed and not attempted, select trial and persist attempted1. On later unconfirmed reset select active. Reject invalid fields before output. The model treats attempted persistence as one atomic record; later projects remove that assumption.
objective_text.T59.04.c: Falsify and transfer: The faulty state machine retries the unconfirmed image forever, causing a boot loop. A watchdog reset alone cannot repair an incorrect persistent selection policy. Then Require two-core health confirmation on H745 and inject one core failing after the other confirms; define a joint image-generation commit and recovery protocol.

checklist: Persist the attempt before jumping, and keep the confirmed image independently recoverable.

sets.title: Redundant journal and torn commit records

objective_text.T59.05.a: Derive and defend: Enumerate crashes after each field write and before/after marker programming. State why the XOR check is a synthetic torn-write control, not an authentication mechanism or robust error code.
objective_text.T59.05.b: Implement and investigate: Implement lc_journal_select over two LCJournal records. A valid record has commit0xa5 and check==seq XOR value XOR0x5a5a5a5a. Select the valid record with greatest nonwrapping seq; equal valid seq with unequal values is ambiguous and rejects. Return selected index through output only on success. Sequence exhaustion requires a migration policy, not wraparound.
objective_text.T59.05.c: Falsify and transfer: Repair selection of an uncommitted newer record and ambiguous equal-generation records. Numerical sequence comparison is invalid after uncontrolled wrap. Then Replace the atomic marker with a multi-byte program unit that can tear; derive a coding/validation rule and prove at least one old or new valid record survives each allowed fault.

sets.title: Monotonic security floor

objective_text.T59.06.a: Derive and defend: Derive the invariant floor never decreases and analyze the confirmation/floor ordering under reset. State the threat model for storage tampering and what a RAM model cannot enforce.
objective_text.T59.06.b: Implement and investigate: Implement lc_raise_floor(current,candidate,confirmed,out): require confirmed exactly1 and candidate>=current; publish candidate on success. Reject rollback or unconfirmed advancement transactionally. Compose it with boot confirmation and identify the trusted persistence needed in real firmware.
objective_text.T59.06.c: Falsify and transfer: The faulty update accepts a smaller floor from an otherwise valid image. A signed image is not permission to weaken anti-rollback policy. Then Introduce a finite monotonic counter that reaches exhaustion; design a fail-closed recovery/key-rotation protocol without silently wrapping its security epoch.

sets.title: Dual-core update quiescence

objective_text.T59.07.a: Derive and defend: Prove no old-generation peer can retain writable storage at update commit. Separate cache visibility, notification delivery and logical acknowledgement.
objective_text.T59.07.b: Implement and investigate: Implement lc_peer_ready(local_epoch,ack_epoch,outstanding) accepting only equal epochs and zero outstanding transfers. Use it in a two-core shutdown model: close admission, drain DMA/IPC owners, obtain an epoch-specific acknowledgement, then permit update. A stale acknowledgement must never unlock a new generation.
objective_text.T59.07.c: Falsify and transfer: Repair acceptance of a stale acknowledgement after independent peer reboot. A memory barrier cannot repair the missing generation check. Then Move shared metadata from noncacheable SRAM to cacheable SRAM; derive cache-line ownership/maintenance and repeat physical traces on the dedicated H745 board.
